articles.title: Ohio man convicted after trying to shoot ex-wife at point-blank range inside restaurant in chilling video
articles.summary: Security video shows Matthew Exton thrusting a handgun at point-blank range near his ex-wife's head inside a Toledo restaurant before a waiter acted.
articles.body: An Ohio man has been convicted of the attempted murder of his ex-wife, whom he tried to shoot last year while she was dining with her family at a restaurant in Toledo, a harrowing incident caught on chilling surveillance video. On April 11, 2025, Matthew Exton, a 43-year-old former attorney, was having a drink at Souk restaurant when he spotted his ex-wife, Kada Malone, dining with her parents at the nearby Italian restaurant Sabira, according to the Lucas County Prosecutor's Office. He entered Sabira, ordered a drink for Malone's table, spat in their direction and walked out. Security footage from the restaurant then shows Exton returning with a handgun before thrusting it to within point-blank range of Malone's head and pulling the trigger as she reacted, putting her hands up in front of her face. The gun failed to fire. LAS VEGAS MAN KILLS EX-WIFE AND HER HUSBAND IN GROCERY STORE AMID CHILD 'CUSTODY ISSUES': POLICE Prosecutors said the gun did fire because the safety was still on. A waiter tackled Exton from behind before he could try to shoot Malone again. Authorities noted that there was a round in the chamber and seven more bullets in the magazine. "The defendant did not come with the intention of having a meal. He came with anger in him and with the intention to commit a public execution of his ex-wife at the restaurant that day," Lucas County Prosecuting Attorney Julia R. Bates said in a statement. "The employees and patrons who stepped in to stop the defendant that day are heroes." Bates also thanked the jury, which found Exton guilty on Sept. 4 of attempted murder, two counts of felonious assault and two firearm specifications attached to all three counts. SPECIAL FORCES VET ACCUSED OF TRYING TO KILL WIFE FOUND DEAD, ENDING MASSIVE TENNESSEE MANHUNT The two counts of felonious assault applied to Malone's parents, Jeannie Malone and Charles Malone. The day the jury handed down their guilty verdict, Exton had an outburst in the courtroom and had to be removed. During the prosecutor's closing arguments, they pointed to a voicemail Exton left for Malone prior to the attempted shooting that referenced the Johnny Cash lyric "Sooner or later God will cut you down," WTOL 11 reported. Prosecutors said the message was an instance of threatening behavior that spoke to Exton's motive and state of mind ahead of the crime. Exton, who appeared to take issue with the prosecutor's framing of the voicemail, then began screaming the lyrics to "God's Gonna Cut You Down" as court officers removed him. At another point, he made a gun-like gesture with his fingers and pointed it at assistant Lucas County Prosecutor Rose Mock. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The jury was instructed by the judge to disregard Exton's conduct and not let it impact their deliberations. Exton, a former lawyer and local prosecutor, is scheduled to be sentenced on Sept. 21, 2026.

articles.title: US court blocks Trump administration plan to cut disaster agency workforce
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he would like to abolish the agency.
articles.body:
A United States federal judge has ruled the Trump administration acted unlawfully by ordering job cuts at the federal agency in charge of responding to the country’s natural disasters.

On Friday, US District Judge Susan Illston in California said the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), exceeded its authority when it ordered personnel changes that effectively stripped the emergency agency of control over its own workforce.

The ruling centres on thousands of temporary FEMA reservists who are called upon to help communities after hurricanes, wildfires, floods and other disasters.

Labor groups representing federal workers sued to block the administration’s decision to stop renewing many of those contracts.

After Hurricane Katrina battered parts of the US Gulf Coast in 2005, the US Congress strengthened FEMA’s independence. US federal law says DHS cannot substantially or significantly reduce the agency’s authority, responsibilities or functions.

Illston, who was appointed by former US President Bill Clinton, said the Trump administration had failed to provide what she described as a “reasoned” explanation for its decision to restrict FEMA’s ability to renew contracts. She also noted FEMA was projecting a workforce of 11,383 employees for the coming fiscal year — about half of its previous level — without a clear justification for the figure.

The dispute comes amid a broader effort by US President Donald Trump’s administration to reduce the size of the federal workforce. Trump has previously questioned the need for FEMA and suggested that states, not the federal government, should assume greater responsibility for disaster preparedness.

The ruling did not immediately order the administration to reverse the cuts or impose penalties. Illston said those issues would be considered in a separate decision expected next month.

articles.title: Death toll in Philippine ferry fire rises to 76 as rescuers recover more remains
articles.summary: Philippine rescuers recovered 41 more charred remains from a ferry fire, authorities said on Saturday, raising the death toll to 76 and leaving 13 people unaccounted for, as forensic teams faced the daunting task of identifying the victims.
articles.body: Philippine rescuers recovered 41 more charred remains from a ferry fire, authorities said on Saturday, raising the death toll to 76 and leaving 13 people unaccounted for, as forensic teams faced the daunting task of identifying the victims. That painstaking process had already begun after 30 bodies recovered on Friday were brought to a port in Coron town, where temporary tents were set up for forensic teams to process and identify the dead. Responders in protective suits were seen carrying black body bags from a Coast Guard vessel into the tents as anxious family members waited nearby for news of their loved ones. One of them was Anelyn Magbanua, 37, whose husband was returning to Coron after visiting their children in Manila when the ferry, which was carrying more than 130 people, caught fire near the end of its more than 20-hour journey. “I hope he is not among the dead being brought off the ship. I hope he is alive and has only drifted to another island,” she said. “It will be very difficult to accept if he’s really gone,” she said. “He loved his children very much.” Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday after extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out, giving authorities access to areas that had been hard to reach because of thick smoke and extreme heat. The Coast Guard said burnt remains were discovered in the ferry’s economy accommodation section. Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel bed frames twisted by intense heat and blanketed in ash. Some photographs appeared to show skeletal remains among the debris. Philippine Coast Guard official Geronimo Tuvilla said at a press conference on Saturday that the immediate priority was to identify the victims and determine the cause of the fire. A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly before the fire broke out. One survivor interviewed by GMA News recalled seeing a small amount of smoke that turned into a fire and quickly spread through the ferry within seconds. Questions also remained over the fate of the vessel’s captain. Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said at the same press conference that she had received information that he was alive, but added that the captain’s name was not on the list of 43 confirmed survivors. The fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands where millions rely on ferries and small boats to travel between provinces and islands.

articles.title: King County wants to spend $100 million on 57 land projects covering about 1,500 acres, from saving part of a city park to turning other sites into salmon habitat and stormwater space
articles.summary: US News: King County Executive Girmay Zahilay has proposed allocating $100 million in conservation funding for 57 projects aimed at expanding urban greenspace,.
articles.body: King County Executive Girmay Zahilay has proposed allocating $100 million in conservation funding for 57 projects aimed at expanding urban greenspace, restoring salmon habitat and protecting farmland, forestland and natural areas across the region.Announced on September 10, the proposal would use existing revenue sources to protect approximately 1,500 acres throughout King County, if approved by the King County Council.$100 million proposal targets parks, farms and salmon habitatAccording to the King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks (DNRP Field Notes), the conservation package includes projects ranging from permanently protecting a popular park in SeaTac and preserving a P-Patch and orchard beside affordable housing in Bellevue to transforming a gravel parking lot along the Duwamish River into salmon habitat.The proposal would also protect farmland that supports the region's local food economy and expand opportunities for trails, recreation and access to natural areas.“One of the most powerful tools we have as a local government to promote healthy, connected, resilient communities throughout King County is land conservation,” Zahilay said.“By protecting these places today, we are building a King County where every generation has access to clean air and water, opportunities for recreation, and pristine natural spaces,” he added.Funding would come from existing revenue sourcesZahilay's proposal is based on recommendations from the 16-member Conservation Futures Advisory Committee, a volunteer board that reviews applications for open-space preservation funding. Its members represent all nine King County Council districts, including urban and rural communities.Of the proposed $100 million, $86.7 million would come from King County's Conservation Futures Program, while another $13.8 million would come from the King County Parks Levy.King County voters approved restoring the Conservation Futures tax to its original rate in 2022, while voters renewed the six-year King County Parks Levy in 2025. Both measures passed with more than 70% of the vote.The 57 projects would contribute to the King County Land Conservation Initiative, a regional effort focused on protecting 65,000 acres of open space, including urban greenspace, farmland, forestland, river corridors, trail corridors and natural areas.Bellevue project would preserve P-Patch next to affordable housingOne proposed project would see the City of Bellevue and Habitat for Humanity preserve a P-Patch and orchard next to an affordable housing development in the Factoria neighborhood.The planned housing development would include 25 units for families with children, while the conservation project would protect the adjacent community garden and orchard.SeaTac park could receive permanent protectionThe City of SeaTac is slated to receive match-waiver funding to permanently protect part of North SeaTac Park, which is among 220 acres of land leased from the Port of Seattle since 1991.The city wants to ensure the property remains a public park despite its designation as “aviation commercial.” The park currently attracts an estimated 650,000 visitors each year.Duwamish River parking lot could become salmon habitatAnother major project would transform a large gravel parking lot in Tukwila along the Duwamish River into habitat for salmon.The project would build on an earlier award that helped acquire the property. Proposed improvements would also include public amenities such as a trail and interpretive signage.The location is important for salmon transitioning between freshwater and saltwater on their journey toward the Pacific Ocean.Nearby, the Chinook Wind restoration project previously converted a paved lot and a deteriorated hotel site into habitat for endangered Chinook salmon, an important food source for southern resident orcas.Eight farms could receive permanent protectionKing County's Department of Natural Resources and Parks would use conservation funding to acquire agricultural conservation easements protecting eight farms on the Enumclaw Plateau and in the Green River Valley.The effort supports King County's Local Food Initiative by preserving farmland that contributes to the region's agricultural economy.The project would also transfer development rights from farmland to urban areas, potentially increasing housing availability while keeping agricultural land protected.Molasses Creek restoration would benefit salmonAnother project would restore Molasses Creek in the Fairwood neighborhood east of Renton.Instead of replacing a deteriorating stormwater pipe beneath a park, King County's Water and Land Resources Division would acquire property to allow the creek to be daylighted, creating a more natural passage for salmon returning to their spawning grounds.A 2023 feasibility study found that daylighting the creek could provide a long-term solution for aging infrastructure while restoring Tier 1 salmon habitat, the county's highest priority for protection and restoration.Other projects include trails, wetlands and stormwater parksThe proposal also includes funding to permanently protect the Lake Youngs Trailhead near Petrovitsky Park, supporting a potential future trail connection.In Skyway, the county plans to acquire property from willing sellers to create a regional stormwater park. The project would provide recreational space while treating runoff from approximately 234 acres before it reaches the Duwamish River.In Duvall, Conservation Futures funding would help expand Big Rock Sports Park, adding protected land between active recreation areas and restored habitat. Plans could include soft-surface trails or a boardwalk along wetlands.Proposal includes $2.1 million for site stabilizationAll land acquisitions funded through Conservation Futures and the King County Parks Levy would be voluntary and require agreements between buyers and sellers.Zahilay's proposal also includes $2.1 million for site stabilization, including demolition and fencing, to ensure newly protected open spaces are safe while improvements begin.Zahilay announced the proposal at Cheryl Chow Park in Seattle's Rainier Valley, where Seattle Parks and Recreation received $2.8 million in Conservation Futures funding to acquire the property. An additional $500,000 from the King County Parks Levy helped cover construction and ADA-accessible playground improvements.The proposal now requires approval from the King County Council before the $100 million conservation package can move forward.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: As Americans are crushed by affordability, mayors push cash handouts as the answer in growing trend
articles.summary: The Economic Securities Project argues cash assistance works best during life transitions as mayors scramble to replace expiring ARPA pandemic aid.
articles.body: A spokesperson for the Economic Securities Project (ESP), an organization that led the creation of more than 100 guaranteed income programs, told Fox News Digital that affordability is creating the "need to bring cash to communities even more urgent." "Further, the destruction of the social safety net paired with skyrocketing costs of healthcare and food have made the need to bring cash to communities even more urgent," ESP's director of cash initiatives, Shafeka Hashash, told Fox News Digital. "Amid the affordability crisis, we have a responsibility to share what we know about cash: that it provides stability, supports economic mobility and helps families move toward a more economically secure future," she added. GUARANTEED INCOME PROGRAM TARGETS LOW-INCOME HOMES LED BY BLACK MOMS AS CASH HANDOUTS SURGE NATIONWIDE As Americans are struggling with rising housing, food and energy costs, both parties are trying to convince voters they have the answer to the affordability crisis ahead of the high-stakes midterm elections. The past holiday weekend was emblematic of ongoing concern over affordability. The AAA estimated that nearly 40 million Americans would pay unprecedented prices for gasoline, making it the most expensive Labor Day holiday at the pump on record. Meanwhile, the ESP has been pushing for guaranteed income long before affordability became a salient issue. Founded in 2016, ESP launched with more than "100 entrepreneurs, activists, researchers, and philanthropists" advocating for direct cash payments. Hashash’s comments came after ESP released a report published Aug. 12 and titled "Right on Time: How Cash Helps Families Move Through Life’s Transitions," making the case for institutionalizing "no-strings-attached" cash assistance. The push comes as city leaders across the nation face a financial cliff. Dozens of municipal mayors are scrambling to maintain local cash-handout experiments as the federal pandemic aid that funded them nears its final spending deadline. CHICAGO SUBURB EXPANDS CASH HANDOUTS AS RACE-BASED REPARATIONS PROGRAM FACES MAJOR LEGAL BATTLE The report's authors build their case by citing "a wealth of data collected from over 250 cash and guaranteed-income pilots across 40 states and the District of Columbia," claiming the findings prove that direct cash transfers are a "legitimate policy tool." However, rather than pushing immediate, universal cash handouts nationwide, the authors suggest a tactical shift of tying direct payments to specific life events. Cash assistance works best during periods of personal or financial hardship, they argued, writing that "cash does its strongest work in moments of transition." The report highlights life events such as having a child, housing relocation or post-incarceration reentry. Hashash told Fox News Digital that the "‘cash for transitions’ memo was not inspired by the lack of federal funding." "It is a reflection of our learnings and observations from more than 250 pilots across 40 states over the past decade. We examined the data and found cash has its greatest impact in moments of transition. These findings are increasingly urgent and resonant across the field as our society collectively grapples with how to approach mass transitions in the face of an increasingly AI-powered economy," she explained. The report pointed to the COVID-19 pandemic as a prime model, calling direct government checks an example of "large-scale transfers" that reached "households at speed and scale." ALBUQUERQUE USES WEED TAX TO FUND 'NO-STRINGS-ATTACHED' GUARANTEED INCOME, SPARKING POLICY DEBATE Advocates and mayors are hoping to transform pandemic-era cash assistance programs into permanent government policy now that federal COVID-19 relief funds are expiring. Under federal law, local governments had until Dec. 31, 2024, to legally obligate their American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, and most obligated funds must be fully spent by Dec. 31, 2026. The broader campaign for direct payments includes Mayors for a Guaranteed Income, led by former Stockton, California, Mayor Michael Tubbs. Tubbs, who launched one of the nation's early municipal cash experiments, has long argued that federal tax dollars should fund income supplements to help lower-income Americans keep up with rising inflation, rent and groceries, claiming it's a viable policy to tackle affordability. DIRECTOR OF 'CASH GIVEAWAY' PROGRAM TAILORED TO NEW MOTHERS GRILLED ON HOW TAXPAYER FUNDING IS USED IN DEBATE In the Chicago suburb of Evanston, Illinois, municipal officials recently announced an expansion of the city's guaranteed income program using the remainder of previously allocated ARPA funds before the spending clock runs out. Evanston is one of more than 100 U.S. municipalities that have launched universal basic income-style pilots since 2018. While many early experiments relied on a blend of private philanthropic dollars and emergency federal stimulus, those coffers are rapidly hitting zero. The looming shortfalls are driving local officials to find alternative avenues to make cash handouts permanent, mirroring recent tax-funded budget maneuvers in neighboring Cook County, Illinois. State affiliates are already moving forward. Economic Security California, an ESP arm, is laying groundwork for state-funded guaranteed income programs. California leads the country in pilot programs, hosting more than 60 cash initiatives to date. To sustain these efforts, ESP recommends that local and state governments look beyond donor funding and establish dedicated revenue streams from local taxes. "We can say, however, that there’s an active and growing movement for cash in hundreds of communities across the country," Hashash said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She added: "We regularly take calls from some of the 1,500 members of the Guaranteed Income Community of Practice – researchers, nonprofits, local government officials, and community leaders all interested in bringing cash to their neighborhoods. We just can’t announce any pilots or policies before the localities do."

articles.title: Who is Emathiio? YouTuber tackled after running onto stage during Roblox CEO’s keynote
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Roblox YouTuber Emathiio was tackled and removed from the Roblox Developers Conference after running onto the stage during CEO David Baszucki's keynot.
articles.body: Roblox YouTuber Emathiio was tackled and removed from the Roblox Developers Conference after running onto the stage during CEO David Baszucki's keynote. The creator was wearing a shirt that said “kids deserve better” when he interrupted the presentation. Security guards quickly stopped Emathiio and escorted him away in front of the audience. The incident came just one day after he uploaded a video strongly criticizing Roblox, its direction, and the platform's ongoing problems with child safety.Who is Emathiio? Roblox YouTuber behind the “kids deserve better” protestEmathiio is a Roblox-focused YouTuber and online creator who has recently been speaking out against the popular gaming platform. There is not much publicly known about his personal life or background, but he appears to be a creator who has become increasingly critical of Roblox and its handling of important issues.On September 10, 2026, Emathiio uploaded a video titled “roblox is completely unfixable.” In the video, he shared his concerns about the direction of Roblox, its relationship with the community, and problems involving child safety.One day later, Emathiio appeared to take his criticism directly to the Roblox Developers Conference, also known as RDC.RDC 2026 took place in San Jose from September 10 to 12. The invite-only event featured Roblox CEO David Baszucki's opening keynote, presentations from creators, and announcements about the future of the platform.However, Baszucki's presentation took an unexpected turn when Emathiio ran toward the stage wearing his “kids deserve better” shirt.YouTuber Emathiio tackled after interrupting Roblox CEO David BaszuckiFootage from the event shows Emathiio running onto the stage during Baszucki's keynote. Security guards quickly moved in and tackled the YouTuber in front of the audience before removing him from the conference area.The video does not clearly show what happened before Emathiio reached the stage. It is also unclear whether he was officially invited to the event or how he was able to get close enough to the stage.At the time of writing, Roblox had not publicly commented on the incident. There was also no public information suggesting that Emathiio had been arrested.The apparent protest comes as Roblox continues to face criticism over child safety. Many creators, parents, and others have raised concerns about how the platform handles predators and inappropriate behavior involving younger users.Roblox has introduced several new safety measures, including age checks, parental tools, and restrictions on communication between some users. However, the company continues to face questions and criticism over whether these changes are enough to protect children.Emathiio's stage interruption appears to be connected to these wider concerns. His shirt and his video uploaded before the event both focused on his belief that Roblox needs to do more for its younger usersCatch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From Portland to Buffalo, these are 5 of the best chicken wing destinations across America
articles.summary: From award-winning sauces in Portland to a legendary Buffalo tavern, these five restaurants serve some of the best chicken wings in America.
articles.body: Saucy, spicy, mild, fried, smoked — however they’re prepared, chicken wings are an American staple, especially during football season. Wings have come a long way since their humble beginnings in Buffalo, New York, where they were popularized in the 1960s. Today, inventive variations have popped up at establishments across the country, some of which have garnered glowing reviews and accolades. The Takeout recently compiled a list of the best chicken wings in every state, with the selections based on multiple factors, including customer reviews, reader polls, local news coverage and wing competitions. Here are five of the best chicken wing destinations across the country, from Oregon to New York. CHICKEN WING PRICES ARE DOWN — HERE'S WHY YOUR FAVORITE RESTAURANT MAY NOT CUT PRICES Fire on the Mountain — Portland, Oregon This locally owned and operated eatery has been around since 2005 and is known for its freshly made, inventive sauces, which are available in unique flavors like Spicy Peanut, Raspberry Habanero and Jamaican Jerk. Its Buffalo Lime Cilantro sauce won first place in the Creative Spicy category at the 2018 National Buffalo Wing Festival, and that same year the restaurant won third place in the Craft Wings category. MEET THE AMERICAN WHO INVENTED BUFFALO WINGS, DISRUPTED ENTIRE CHICKEN INDUSTRY Fire on the Mountain also offers a rotating "sauce of the month," as well as vegan wings. Scovilles — Salt Lake City, Utah The Scoville scale measures the spiciness of chili peppers so, as the name suggests, Scovilles in Salt Lake City likes to bring the heat. Guests can choose from an array of sauces and dry rubs, including Scotch Bonnet, Ghost Pepper, Carolina Reaper and more spicy selections. Those who don’t love extreme heat opt for milder flavors like Cajun Honey BBQ and Buffalo Cilantro Lime. Scovilles earned the title of "Best Wings" in Salt Lake City Weekly’s 2025 "Best of Utah" awards, with the write-up raving about the wings’ crispiness and sauciness. AMERICA'S BIGGEST BEER-LOVING STATES REVEALED — SEE WHERE YOURS RANKS Wings, Etc. — Topeka, Kansas This Topeka restaurant is no stranger to the chicken wing spotlight. Its wings were crowned "Best Wings" by the Topeka Capital-Journal’s Community Choice for five years in a row, from 2020 through 2024. It was also awarded the title of "Twisted Wing King" at the Topeka Wing Fling in 2021, thanks to its Buffalo sauce and lime-pepper rub hybrid. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Customers love the Hot-Honey Garlic and Tweener sauces at Wings Etc., The Takeout noted. Ale Emporium — Indianapolis, Indiana CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Serving Indianapolis since 1982, one of the Ale Emporium’s most popular items is the Hermanaki wing, a crispy, sweet and spicy jumbo wing covered in a secret spice blend, along with the restaurant’s special house sauce and teriyaki. Ale Emporium does the classics well, too: Its Buffalo wings were praised by Axios Indianapolis in 2024. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Bar-Bill Tavern — Buffalo, New York Would a chicken wing round-up really be complete without mentioning Buffalo? Home of the Buffalo wing, the city has no shortage of places to get a wing fix. Although Bar-Bill Tavern is not where the Buffalo wing was originally created, it is a spot that holds its own and serves up some of the best wings in the area, according to locals and Visit Buffalo Niagara. articles.title: ‘Woman Unknown’ wins Golden Lion, Malkovich ‘humbled’ by best actor award at Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: VENICE, Italy — “Woman Unknown,” a drama about Denmark in the aftermath of the Nazi occupation directed by May el-Toukhy, won the prestigious Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival on Saturday.
articles.body: VENICE, Italy — “Woman Unknown,” a drama about Denmark in the aftermath of the Nazi occupation directed by May el-Toukhy, won the prestigious Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival on Saturday. The Maggie Gyllenhaal -led jury announced the winners, which included a best actor prize for John Malkovich for his performance in the dark CIA comedy “Wild Horse Nine.” Malkovich was not in attendance at the ceremony, but he sent a video message, explaining that he is shooting in Montreal. “I am humbled to be chosen for this award which has been given to so many wonderful actors,” Malkovich said. Only 8 women have won a Golden Lion El-Toukhy, who was the only woman to have solely directed a film in the main competition this year, is the eighth woman to have won the festival’s top prize. “To me personally, ‘Woman Unknown’ is about the female body as a battleground,” el-Toukhy said. “At the same time the film tells the tale of women who are unseen, invisible and voiceless.” She thanked Gyllenhaal for using her voice to shine a light on unequal opportunities for women in moviemaking. The film, which does not yet have distribution in North America, is centered on a young nanny and housemaid who is about to marry her wealthy employer in the immediate aftermath of the war. But she harbors a secret past intimate relationship with a German soldier that threatens to upend her reputation. The lead, Mathilde Arcel, won the festival’s best actress prize. Arcel was visibly emotional as she accepted the award, which she placed on the floor as she spoke as she said it was very heavy. “This is my first lead role in a movie and my first time at a film festival,” she said. “I’m extremely honored.” South Korean auteur Lee Chang-dong’s poetic portrait of class and labor, “Possible Love,” won the Silver Lion grand jury prize. “Possible Love” is Lee’s first film in eight years, following his acclaimed “Burning.” “We are living in an era where the meaning of labor is fading and human connections are increasingly becoming severed,” Lee said through a translator. “I made this film to ask what cinema can and should do in times like these. I take this award as a sign that you want me to keep asking these questions.” Gaza documentary takes special jury prize “NAZA,” a harrowing documentary about military strategies employed in the war in Gaza from Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, was awarded a special jury prize. “It’s honestly not very easy to stand here, thinking of all the people, the Israeli politicians, the journalists back home who are attacking this film, denying it without even seeing it,” Abraham said. “It is really, really especially important to us that Israelis watch this film.” The was added to the main competition late — at the request of the filmmakers — and debuted late in the schedule as well, but its impact was felt as it received a record-breaking standing ovation, lasting some 25 minutes, after its premiere. Shot on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night in extreme secrecy over three years, “NAZA” features testimony from 24 Israeli military insiders including intelligence officers and soldiers give who insight into the war in Gaza and what they say is the systemic killing of Palestinian civilians. The jury gave the Silver Lion for directing to Ilya Krzhanovsky for his film “Dau,” a project about the Soviet physicists who built the atomic bomb that has taken over 20 years to make. Krzhanovsky, who renounced his Russian citizenship in protest of the war in Ukraine, dedicated the prize to Ukrainians, including his mother who was born there. French director Stéphane Brizé’s won the screenplay prize for his corporate drama “A Good Little Soldier.” Malou Khebizi was given the Marcello Mastroianni award for emerging actor for her role in Cédric Kahn’s “A Place to Heal,” which is set in an adolescent psychiatric ward in a public hospital. The jury this year included “The Voice of Hind Rajab” director Kaouther Ben Hania, English composer Daniel Blumberg, French filmmaker Xavier Giannoli, Afghan filmmaker Shahrbanoo Sadat and Hong Kong filmmaker Johnnie To. Malkovich’s Oscar chances just went up Aside from Malkovich’s win, the starrier, Hollywood films playing in competition were shut out of the awards, including “Primetime,” “Bunker” and “Ink.” Some look to the Venice Film Festival awards for early indications of who might be in with a shot at Oscar nominations and wins. In recent years, Venice has launched winning best actor campaigns for people like Brendan Fraser and Adrien Brody. Malkovich has yet to win an Oscar.

articles.title: Second crypto billionaire donates record $49m to far-right Reform UK
articles.summary: The two donations increase the total sum of money pledged to Reform since Friday to $97m.
articles.body:
A second British billionaire has made a record donation of almost $49m to the far-right Reform UK party , matching the amount pledged by another businessman the day before.

Writing in the Daily Telegraph British newspaper on Saturday, donor Christopher Harborne said the $48.7m (£36m) donation was a “philanthropic gift” to the country, adding that he felt “inspired” to match the contribution made by fellow billionaire Ben Delo 24 hours earlier.

Sixty-three-year-old Harborne is a Thailand-based cryptocurrency investor and Delo, 42, is the co-founder of the BitMEX cryptocurrency exchange.

Both donations bring the total sum of money pledged to Reform since Friday to $97m.

They coincide with a flurry of questions surrounding the party’s finances, with London’s Metropolitan Police confirming earlier this week the launch of a criminal investigation into whether Reform accepted illegal foreign donations.

Reform’s leader Nigel Farage celebrated the contributions in a post on X.

“You know what Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne want? Nothing,” Farage said.

“Just a government that will fix Britain. And that’s what Reform UK will deliver,” he added.

The leader of the right-wing Conservative Party, Kemi Badenoch, criticised Reform, accusing Farage and his colleagues of lacking integrity.

“You can buy staff and advertising, but you can’t buy judgement or integrity,” Badenoch posted on X.

“Sometimes a bigger cheque just means you make more of the same mistakes. The Conservatives are up for the fight.”

Reform has emerged as a major political force in the UK. However, the latest polling data suggests that the party has lost some voters since left-leaning Andy Burnham replaced Keir Starmer as prime minister and Labour Party leader.

Reporting from London, Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec said both of Reform’s latest donors believe they are making British politics fairer.

“One of the reasons that Ben Delo gave for this huge record-breaking donation was to level the political playing field,” Nedelec said.

“That’s certainly a sentiment echoed by fellow billionaire Christopher Harborne, who compared Reform UK to a startup in need of a boost, because unlike the mainstream political parties, it doesn’t benefit from this inbuilt infrastructure of financial support and recurring donations.

“They certainly see this as a way of making British politics fairer. If we zoom out, Reform historically has had very few donations compared to the mainstream political parties,” she added.

Reform is the successor to Farage’s Brexit Party, which changed its name to Reform in 2021. Farage, who played a significant role in the Brexit movement, has long portrayed himself as an anti-establishment figure and has experienced a surge in popularity as voters grow increasingly disillusioned with the Conservatives and Labour. The two parties have historically dominated British politics, but a dramatic decline in living standards in recent years has fuelled demand for alternatives.

articles.title: Planned Powys rail centre not built despite £70m spend
articles.summary: The site has not found private-sector funding because the risk is "too great," its boss says.
articles.body:
The future of a proposed rail-testing centre that has received £70m of taxpayers' money but still has not been built is to be decided by the Welsh government.

The Global Centre of Rail Excellence (GCRE) has not found the private-sector funding it needs as the risk is "too great" for potential investors, its boss has said.

Launched five years ago, the project is based at the former Nant Helen opencast coal mine near Ystradgynlais, Powys.

Ministers are now being asked to approve plans for a data centre there, which GCRE hopes will attract more funding for the rail project.

The Welsh government said GCRE – which it owns – has been "exploring a range of projects to revitalise" the site.

"We are working with the company to assess next steps, in light of our productivity mission," a spokesperson added.

The Welsh government has given GCRE £50m since it was set up by Labour in 2021.

The former Conservative UK government also provided £20m.

GCRE hoped to find £330m from private backers to transform the mine near Bannau Brycheiniog national park - also known as the Brecon Beacons.

Two 4.3 mile (7km) electrified tracks for testing trains would loop around a site roughly the size of Gibraltar.

With other facilities, GCRE said it could create more than 1,000 jobs.

It was supposed to be up and running in 2025, but has been delayed until 2030.

The scheme was inherited by Plaid Cymru when it won the Senedd election in May.

GCRE chief executive Simon Jones said there was demand in the rail industry for the services the company would provide "but we can't carry on using public money on this forever so a decision needs to be made".

Jones added that there had been "detailed conversations" with an energy and data centre company, but said he could not name it due to commercial confidentiality.

GCRE wants to complete those talks this year so a contract can be signed.

"And we need to be in a position where we know whether the railway is going ahead or not at the moment we sign that contract," he told BBC Politics Wales .

"If the government decides this is something that it wants to do, if we are able to execute the contract with the data centre partner, then five years from now we could be in a situation where we see trains running around this site."

GCRE has spoken to potential investors around the world, but failed to secure funding.

"I can list off a whole load of what would sound like excuses about macro-economic conditions, the long tail of Covid, etcetera, but essentially it comes down to risk appetite from the investment market," Jones said.

"This is an unknown proposition that we have got here. There is risk around being able to create the UK's first purpose-built high speed rail testing facility, and that risk is too great for the market to take on its own in current circumstances."

Welsh Conservative Member of the Senedd Andrew RT Davies, who visited the site as chairman of the last Senedd's economy committee, said: "The government needs to get its act together, make a quick decision.

"Is it going to continue to back this site for regeneration purposes or is it going to re-purpose it for other reasons?"

articles.title: More Americans are dining alone as solo restaurant reservations soar, data shows
articles.summary: Solo restaurant reservations surged 22% year over year, according to Toast data, as dining alone sheds its stigma and reshapes the industry.
articles.body: A table for one is becoming more common in the dining scene, with solo reservations reportedly spiking in recent years. Reservations for one surged 22% year over year in the third quarter of 2025, according to restaurant technology company Toast’s latest trends report, suggesting that dining alone may be losing its stigma. Single-diner bookings still accounted for less than 1% of total reservations, according to Toast, but industry experts say it reflects a broader shift and opportunity in the restaurant world. The trend was also evident in the af&co. and Carbonate 2024 Hospitality Trends Report, which cited Brandwatch data showing interest in eating as a party of one had increased 7% year over year. WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS ARE CHANGING DINING AS CUSTOMERS EAT HALF THEIR MEALS, TAKE REST HOME, CELEBRITY CHEF SAYS "People stopped waiting for someone else to be free," Stephen Ingber, owner of Denver private-chef and catering company MileHighCook, told Fox News Digital. "A good meal used to require a date or a group to justify it. Now it just requires a reservation." Ingber said about 15% of his bookings are now for one guest and that has risen annually. Some solo customers even book weekly or monthly, he added, and are often the best kind of customer. Solo dining has also grown across both quick-service and full-service restaurants, as more consumers, especially Gen Z and millenials, embrace meals centered on convenience and personal enjoyment, Fox News Digital previously reported. RESTAURANTS BAN DINERS' PHONES DURING MEALS AS NO-SCROLL TREND GROWS: PUT IT AWAY OR ELSE "It's a small slice that is growing fast," agreed Terry Psaltakis, a 30-year restaurant operator from Chicago and founder of ShiftTrained. Experts say restaurants that offer bar seating, smaller tables with a view, wine by the glass or half-bottle options and menus that do not assume sharing are best for solo diners. EX-WAITRESS REVEALS RESTAURANT TIPPING SECRET MOST CUSTOMERS DON'T REALIZE — EXPERT CALLS IT 'BAD HOSPITALITY' Just as important, Psaltakis said, is giving solo guests the same care and service as larger parties. Without company to distract them, they are there solely for the dining experience. "Get it right and that solo diner turns into a regular who comes back every week and knows your bartender by name," Psaltakis said. For diners who feel self-conscious, Ingber and Psaltakis both recommend the bar. "Ask the bartender what they’d order," he said. "A good one, a ready one, lights up." COWBOY CHEF SAYS PHONES AND SCREENS AT DINNER ARE TEARING AMERICAN FAMILIES APART Dining alone isn't always a sign of loneliness, Rene Mondy, a Georgia-based licensed grief therapist and founder of The Solo Dining Directory, told Fox News Digital. "Solo diners in healthy relationships seem to understand that dining with a partner or surrounded by friends doesn’t always equal connection," Mondy said. While some diners might be hungry for conversation, others might relish in the alone time, Ingber said. He recommended using the experience as an opportunity to order something you might avoid with company or on a date, and not hiding behind a phone or book. articles.title: Summit success gives BJP a boost in domestic politics
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India's success against the odds in bringing Brics countries with incongruent, even conflicting, outlooks on key global issues of contentio.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's success against the odds in bringing Brics countries with incongruent, even conflicting, outlooks on key global issues of contention, such as the West Asia conflict, to throw their weight behind a joint declaration comes as a timely domestic boost for BJP when its rivals are sensing some vulnerability in its otherwise dominant political position.Foreign policy has been a major component of BJP's arsenal in scoring political points over its rivals, especially Congress, as it has projected a rising global profile of an assertive India under PM Narendra Modi's leadership, in contrast to the country's "meek" response to challenges from external security to trade in the pre-2014 period.Modi hailed the New Delhi Declaration, adopted unanimously at Brics, saying confidence of the bloc is wider in reach and stronger in purpose.With BJP marshalling a counter-offensive against the opposition and set to step up its public connect with a month-long campaign from Modi's birthday (Sept 17), the Brics outcome will be one more arrow in its quiver. The photograph of Modi holding the hand of Iran's President Masoud and leading him into Bharat Mandapam, the fact that Indian diplomacy was crucial in getting Iran and its rival the UAE to sign the declaration as well as the tough formulation against coercive tariff and unilateral sanctions can only blunt opposition's criticism about diminished strategic autonomy because of pressure from US. That the resolution did not mention US by name does not take away much from the perception of India holding its own at the summit which the Trump administration must have been watching closely.All this is a perfect fit for Modi's "strong leader" brand.The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration in 2023, with a gulf separating Russia and the West over invasion of Ukraine too, had come amid a cloud of uncertainty over such a possibility. Working with others, India somehow conjured up a document that was unanimously adopted. The diplomatic success became a major talking point for NDA in the run-up to the 2024 elections.A similar success at Brics attests to the governing alliance's contention that India now enjoys a standing that can persuade global leaders to get around their differences to thrash out a consensus outcome.In his post on X on the declaration, Modi said with the document's focus on innovation, sustainability, people-to-people ties and more, the endeavour is to make cooperation practical, development-oriented and responsive to the aspirations of Brics nations.BJP was quick to drive home its message. Its president Nitin Nabin said Bharat has once again demonstrated its commitment to a more representative and balanced world.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump: US president's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted an audience across the Atlantic
articles.summary: Nobody could have predicted that today's main global headline would be Trump's desire to see a unified Ireland.
articles.body:
When another world leader meets US President Donald Trump the only certainty about what might happen is the uncertainty about what might happen.

This was exactly the case ahead of President Trump's two-day visit to Ireland.

Nobody could have predicted that by the end of the first day, the main global headline would be his desire to see a unified Ireland .

As the shockwaves of his remarks rippled through this island and Great Britain, it was unclear whether this represented a new US administration policy, or an off-the-cuff remark from a president who likes to take questions from reporters, and likes to give answers.

Former Republican Congressman Mick Mulvaney was Trump's special envoy to Northern Ireland in his first term in office.

He cautioned against anyone reading too much into the president's remarks.

"This does not represent a shift in US foreign policy," he said.

"We're still very much committed to the Good Friday Agreement."

Democratic Congressman Brendan Boyle agreed.

"There is bipartisan support for that deal, and that is not going to change."

Although both agreed that Donald Trump was probably right to say that "eventually" unification would happen, that did not mean the US was about to start pushing for it.

Giving an answer to a question that is asked at a free-flowing press conference is one thing, but Donald Trump repeated his sentiments a short time later when he was delivering a speech to an invited audience at the US Ambassador's residence.

In fact it was almost the first thing he mentioned, hinting that maybe he realised he had kicked over a can of worms at his earlier appearance.

The rest of that speech was curious. It was billed as a 20-minute address to Irish and Irish American business leaders, but was about twice that and strayed largely into domestic US matters.

President Trump has a speaking style that he describes himself as "the weave".

He can bounce from topic to topic during any speaking engagement, veering off the script and then returning to the matter at hand.

Today he lauded his own achievements, as he sees them, such as clamping down on illegal immigration, doing deals and boosting defence production.

He repeated his criticisms once again of what he views as the UK's lack of support for his military operation in Iran.

But who was his target audience? The gathered business leaders in Dublin or a US audience tuning in before it was even dawn in much of that country?

This November's crunch midterm elections are fast approaching and the Republican party is under intense pressure because of the president's policies.

They may lose control of one or both houses of Congress.

About one tenth of the US population claim Irish heritage but they are not a homogeneous voting bloc.

Was he trying to target Irish-American independent or swing voters in the US, of which there are many who have flip-flopped between the Republican and Democratic party in recent years?

Some of them do support a unified Ireland and so in this time of chasing every vote, perhaps that played a part.

Bill Clinton secured a lot of Irish-American support when he was running for president, by promising to get engaged in the peace process.

They voted for him and he followed through on his promise and much of that work led to the foundations of the Good Friday Agreement.

But, Irish America is a different place now. Indeed, America is a different place now as politics have become more polarised.

The November election campaigns show no indication that will change anytime soon.

But political leaders in Ireland will be hoping the only debate tomorrow is about the play on the golf course.

articles.title: Modi: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any long.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer and that the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership".Modi focused on economic integration of the Global South in his address at the session on inclusive governance and multilateralism, saying the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers."The Global South today stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making," the PM said, proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform.Modi positions Brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forumThese should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said. He sought a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake and the development of humanity remains at the centre of all endeavours”.On representation, he said UNSC reform can no longer be delayed and text-based negotiations on this subject must be tied to a fixed timeline and clear outcomes. “Similarly, voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within global financial institutions must reflect today’s economic realities. Countries driving global economic growth deserve an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,” he added.While western experts have often described Brics as an anti-West forum, Modi said the grouping operates not against anyone, but with an inclusive approach that brings everyone along. “Today, Brics is also in its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus,” he said.The PM called upon the bloc to work on an ambitious new agenda, translating its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage. He proposed establishment of a Brics Continuity and Implementation Mechanism. “Brics presidency changes every year, but this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. Under this mechanism, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the troika (past, current and incoming presidency),” said Modi.Raising the issue of seafarers’ safety, Modi talked about how they make a massive contribution to global trade and yet lack adequate support in difficult times. He proposed creating a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect maritime authorities and missions of relevant nations. “This network would assist with distress alerts, medical aid, family notifications and evacuation efforts.”He said ensuring equal participation in setting the global rules of the future is critical. “AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also future rules. We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers,” he said. “The message of this Brics summit must be clear: if our future is shared, the right to shape it must also be shared,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Who was ‘El Piturris,’ the Mexican influencer killed in Sonora?
articles.summary: José Luis Esparza Güicho was a popular podcaster who shared funny stories of everyday life while working at his family’s taco restaurant.
articles.body: Years before he was killed in the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora, the influencer José Luis Esparza Güicho came to be known as “El Piturris.” The nickname originated from one time during his childhood when Esparza’s father came home drunk, Luis Antonio Escalante, the producer of Esparza’s podcast, told CNN. His father tried to call Esparza by the name “Pirruris,” a famous television character at the time. Instead, he drunkenly called him “Piturris.” “Then, as a joke among the other family members, ‘Piturris’ stuck,” Escalante said. Many years after that story, this would still be the nickname by which Esparza was known — not only within his family, but also on social media and on his podcast La Guarida, which had launched one year ago. Luis Alberto González, who is called “Huicho,” is the show’s co-host and Esparza’s friend for more than two decades. He says it was always easy to work with Esparza to record the episodes, in which they shared their life experiences and exchanged jokes. “It was easy because Piturris, more than anything, wasn’t a character. He was a person whose anecdotes, stories and everything he told on the podcast were real; they were people’s lived experiences,” González told CNN. “I think we were successful because things happen to all of us in life, but we look at them differently by laughing at what happens to us. You tell what happens to you every day as a joke, and people identify with it,” he said. The latest episode of La Guarida featuring both hosts was posted on YouTube on Wednesday and received more than 34,000 views. On Thursday night, hours after Esparza was killed, Escalante said in a video that they had already recorded two more episodes, which will be released in the coming days. From the family business to social media Esparza was 37 years old and the father of a young boy. He was active on Facebook and Instagram, where he shared images of his family, humorous content, and videos of himself singing banda music or visiting public places. Over time, his content gained traction, reaching a combined audience of 130,000 followers on both accounts as of Saturday. González says Esparza was very outgoing from a young age and liked spending time with older people. Escalante says that when they began developing plans to launch La Guarida, they thought of Esparza as a host because he was “easygoing” and people liked him. Before becoming an influencer, Esparza worked in the family business: a taco restaurant located in downtown Ciudad Obregón, a city in the southern part of Mexico’s Sonora state. Esparza’s family ran the restaurant, called Los Güichos, for about 50 years, as it became very well known among locals, Escalante said. Even while growing as a content creator, Esparza continued working at the restaurant. The business would also become the site of his killing. On Thursday morning, an armed man arrived at the establishment and shot Esparza, before fleeing on a motorcycle with another person, according to the Sonora Attorney General’s Office. On Friday, the Attorney General’s Office said it was investigating a possible connection between Esparza’s death and another killing that occurred Wednesday in the nearby town of Cócorit, in which the target was a relative of Esparza by marriage who allegedly wrote songs for a criminal organization. “Based on this information, one of the main lines of investigation is that the homicide may be related to a confrontation between criminal groups linked to drug trafficking. The Attorney General’s Office is continuing its investigation to determine the involvement of those responsible,” the office said in a statement. ‘Keep your spirits up’ Esparza’s death is the latest case in a series of murders of Mexican influencers over at least the past two years. There is no official record of how many influencers have been killed in Mexico. According to a CNN tally, there have been nine cases in the state of Sinaloa alone since 2024, while others have been recorded in states such as Baja California, Jalisco and Morelos. As the investigation into Esparza’s killing moves forward, a memorial Mass was held on Friday. His friends and colleagues continue to express their condolences. In a video posted to social media on Thursday night, Escalante offered his condolences to Esparza’s family and said that the La Guarida team would take some time off. “What we did was spread joy, and we need to heal and be well before we can continue our work,” he said, his voice breaking as he recalled a phrase Esparza often used to end his videos: “Keep your spirits up.” González also remembers those words, which he considers emblematic of the friend with whom he shared the microphone. “His motto was ‘Keep your spirits up.’ That was his motto, because he was a taco vendor… he was a taco vendor who looked at life and lived like someone who lacked nothing, even though he did face hardships,” he said. “On every podcast, he would crack open a large bottle of beer, and his motto was to keep your spirits up, you don’t need much to be happy. You can have 99 problems, and if you have just one reason to be happy, that’s enough,” González said.
